findings.evidence: "every control has a non-empty accessible name (icon-only included) ...; every action works by keyboard; WCAG AA contrast in every theme the screen ships": the model already knows these WCAG basics; only the fail lines (24 px targets, 3:1 non-text including focus rings, SC 2.5.3 label-in-name) are new to it
findings.fix: Cut the a11y Rule to the non-obvious fail lines: 'Fail: an accessible name that drops the visible word (SC 2.5.3); non-text contrast under 3:1 in any shipped theme (input borders, icons, focus rings); targets under 24x24 CSS px (44 is a design target, not the fail line).' Leave the generic WCAG duties to the model.

findings.evidence: "**Review and fix**: Review steps, then Build steps on the failed rows.": nothing says which failed rows to fix first when several fail and some fixes change the layout that other fixes sit on
findings.fix: Add one ordering line: 'Fix failed rows in this order: states and loading (they change the layout), then responsive, tokens and consistency, then hierarchy, a11y and interaction; re-check earlier rows after each layout change.'

findings.evidence: "Pass: no color, type, spacing, radius or shadow literal in a component": no gotcha says whether `0`, `100%`, `transparent`, `currentColor` or `inherit` count as literals, so two reviewers can split on the tokens row
findings.fix: Add a Gotcha: 'Tokens exempts `0`, percentages, `auto`, `inherit`, `currentColor` and `transparent`: they encode no brand value, so a rebrand or dark theme never needs to change them.'

findings.evidence: "load the file for each rule ... whose verdict turns on an exception there (2.5.8 target exceptions, container queries, worked hierarchy calls)": the agent cannot tell whether a verdict depends on an exception it has not read yet, so this trigger is circular
findings.fix: Name concrete triggers: 'Read references/rules/a11y.md when a target under 24 px might be inline text or spaced from its neighbours; responsive.md when a container query sets the width; hierarchy.md when two filled buttons may sit in separate panels or a repeated list.'

findings.evidence: "on a tie, fill the one Enter triggers (the form submit), else the first in reading order": a fixed tie-breaker for a product-emphasis call, with no fallback to asking the user or following product intent
findings.fix: Keep it as the default and add an escape hatch: '...else the first in reading order, unless the user or product brief names the preferred action; state the choice in the hand-over.'

findings.evidence: "a MUI `Button` already has one, so add none": followed through on the review-dashboard eval, the interaction row should pass for an MUI `IconButton`. The skill names only `Button`, and the verdict table says a `:focus-visible` ring is established by source, so an agent could leave the IconButton row as na
findings.fix: Extend the gotcha: 'MUI `Button`, `IconButton` and other ButtonBase controls ship a focus-visible ripple/ring; in source they establish interaction unless `disableRipple` or `disableFocusRipple` removes it with no replacement.'

findings.evidence: The passing example repeats standard fetch/Promise/conditional-JSX mechanics: "fetch('/api/orders')" and ".then((r) => { if (!r.ok) throw new Error(String(r.status)); return r.json(); })". Several rule sections likewise activate familiar UI practices rather than supply new expertise; the strongest knowledge delta is the evidence protocol, exceptions and framework gotchas.
findings.fix: Replace the routine fetch/JSX walkthrough with a shorter delta example focused on retry clearing the error, the initially empty live region and MUI skeleton geometry. Keep the enforceable rule criteria concise rather than expanding familiar UI practices.

findings.evidence: "renders at all four widths that show neither pass" permits a responsive pass after testing only 360, 768, 1280 and 1920 px. However, references/rules/responsive.md:7 explicitly identifies 320 CSS px as a reflow fail line. A page that fits at 360 px but clips at 320 px therefore reaches conflicting outcomes, and the opening instruction says nothing outside the Rule and Trap fails a row.
findings.fix: Add an explicit 320 CSS px reflow branch to the main responsive rule and Render workflow, align the source-based width checks with it, and require that observation before passing. Retain the existing four widths as additional layout checks.

findings.evidence: "a custom sx that sets outline: none or overrides '&:focus-visible' removes them" incorrectly treats either declaration as sufficient to remove MUI's focus indication. With the default ripple enabled, outline: none alone does not remove the focus ripple; adding a :focus-visible rule also does not inherently remove existing indication.
findings.fix: Fail only when the actual focus indication is removed without a replacement. Distinguish outlines from MUI's ripple and .Mui-focusVisible styling, inspect the declarations being overridden, and retain the separate disableRipple warning.

findings.evidence: "Write the pending, empty, error and success branches before polish" is unconditional in Build steps. Following it for the bundled dismissible-banner or checkout-action-row scenarios demands asynchronous state machinery even though those requests establish no asynchronous operation.
findings.fix: Gate this step on actual asynchronous work: write applicable pending, empty, error and success branches when the component starts or consumes a request; otherwise skip them and implement only the local interaction states the task needs.
